title: One-step update of the work-tape window
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a symbol alphabet, let $M$ be a Turing machine with finitely many states and $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be an input word, and let $t,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $a\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $n>0$. At time $t$, every work-tape head is at a coordinate in $[a,a+n)$, every tape cell outside this interval is blank, every coordinate in the interval has been visited by some work-tape head at some time at most $t$, and every work-tape head stayed in the interval throughout times $0$ through $t$. Suppose also that $n\le 2t+1$. Let $\alpha$ be an action such that the configuration at time $t+1$ is obtained by applying $\alpha$ to the configuration at time $t$. Let $\ell,r\in\{0,1\}$, with $\ell=1$ exactly when some work-tape head at coordinate $a$ is instructed by $\alpha$ to move left, and $r=1$ exactly when some work-tape head at coordinate $a+n-1$ is instructed by $\alpha$ to move right. Then at time $t+1$, every work-tape head lies in $[a-\ell,a-\ell+n+r+\ell)$, every tape cell outside this interval is blank, every coordinate in it has been visited by some work-tape head by time $t+1$, and every work-tape head stayed in it throughout times $0$ through $t+1$. The new interval has positive integer width $n+r+\ell\le 2(t+1)+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $\Gamma$ is a symbol alphabet; $M$ has finitely many states and $k$ work tapes; $x$ is an input word.
$t,n$ are natural numbers and $a$ is an integer.
At time $t$, all work-tape heads lie in $[a,a+n)$.
At time $t$, all tape cells outside $[a,a+n)$ are blank.
Every coordinate in $[a,a+n)$ was visited by a work-tape head at some time at most $t$.
At every time from $0$ through $t$, all work-tape heads lie in $[a,a+n)$.
The configuration at time $t+1$ is the result of applying the given action to the time-$t$ configuration.
$\ell$ is true exactly when an action-directed leftward move occurs from coordinate $a$.
$r$ is true exactly when an action-directed rightward move occurs from coordinate $a+n-1$.
